title: AR, The new frontier in remote work
excerpt: How augmented reality is changing remote assistance, design reviews and onboarding for distributed teams.

author.name: Boyo Martínez
author.bio: Boyo leads product and design at NicaSource, where he helps US companies plan, staff and run nearshore engineering teams. He has spent fifteen years shipping digital products with distributed teams across the Americas.

meta.body:
Introduction

Augmented reality is moving out of the demo room and into the daily work of distributed teams. Headsets and phone-based AR now let a remote engineer see what an on-site colleague sees, annotate it and walk them through a fix.

Why now

Lighter hardware, better spatial anchors and real-time collaboration SDKs have made AR practical for everyday work, not just trade-show booths.

Where AR Helps Remote Teams

Remote assistance

Field technicians share their view with an expert hundreds of miles away, who draws directly on the equipment in front of them. First-time fix rates go up and travel goes down.

Spatial design reviews

Product and industrial designers review 3D prototypes together at full scale, from different countries, without shipping a single physical model.

Onboarding and training

Step-by-step overlays turn tribal knowledge into repeatable procedures that a new hire can follow on day one.

Challenges to Plan For

  • Bandwidth: shared AR sessions need stable, low-latency connections on both ends.
  • Privacy: cameras in the workplace need clear policies about what is recorded and stored.
  • Wellbeing: long sessions cause fatigue; keep immersive work in short, focused blocks.

The best AR tools disappear: people stop talking about the headset and start talking about the problem.

Conclusion

AR will not replace video calls, but it fills the gap where words and screenshots fail. Teams that build the skills now, including nearshore engineers who can develop and support these tools, will be ready when it becomes standard.
